v.why: Smaller batches give many more Adam updates per epoch, which rescues low-LR underfitting within 243 epochs.
The optimal LR shrinks with width, so widening at an already high LR overshoots and destabilizes training.
Large batches give few updates, and wider nets extract more progress per step.
Over-parameterized wide nets overfit and benefit more from stronger weight decay.
Small batches mean many more steps, so cumulative L2 shrinkage is larger and strong alpha over-shrinks.
Deeper nets train more slowly at tiny LR and stay undertrained in 243 epochs.
Depth substitutes for missing width in narrow nets, while in wide nets extra layers are redundant.
Strong L2 compounds across more layers and shrinks the signal toward underfitting.
Large batches take few steps with low gradient noise, so a higher LR is both needed and tolerated.
Depth-3 nets have compounding sensitivity to large steps, so a higher LR risks divergence.
